hints: A product is a square exactly when every prime exponent is even.
Represent each number by the parity of its prime exponents.
Count subsets whose parity vectors XOR to zero using a linear basis.
analogy: Even numbers of every prime factor cancel like pairs of switches.
example: For [2,2,3,6], the square-product subsets are the empty set, the two 2s, [2,3,6] using either 2: 4 in total.
algorithm: Sieve primes up to 5000 and factor every number. Build a bit vector with a 1 for primes occurring an odd number of times. Insert all vectors into a Gaussian-elimination XOR basis over GF(2), counting the rank r. Output 2^(n-r) modulo 1000000007, including the empty subset.
correctness: The product is a square exactly when the XOR of the chosen parity vectors is zero. Choosing a subset is a binary vector mapped linearly to its parity sum. A rank-r linear map on n binary choices has a kernel of dimension n-r and therefore exactly 2^(n-r) zero-sum subsets.
complexity: For n values at most 5000 and p primes up to 5000, bitset Gaussian elimination uses O(n*p^2/w) word operations in a simple implementation, O(p^2/w) words of space, plus factoring; w is the machine word size.
